summary: The biggest story of this run is TRANSCEND-T2D-2, the first Phase 3 head-to-head trial of retatrutide against semaglutide 2 mg. Lilly released topline results on Oct 28 (~10:45 GMT), and ABC, Reuters, STAT, NY Post and Everyday Health all covered it within 24 h. I checked the numbers against HCPLive and AJMC. The trial enrolled 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor. It was open-label and randomized 2:2:1. At 80 weeks, using the 'if everyone stayed on treatment' measure, A1C fell 2.2 points on retatrutide 9 or 12 mg vs 1.8 on semaglutide. Weight fell 19.5% (9 mg) and 20.9% (12 mg) vs 9.4%. Stopping because of side effects: 4.8% and 7.9% vs 2.7%. Dysesthesia (unusual skin sensations): 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%. The results are not peer-reviewed yet. TIMING FLAG: the next 14:00 ET long-form slot (Oct 30) is about 55 h after first report, so it misses the 48 h Lane C rule by about 7 h, and the trial has no tirzepatide arm. The Editor-in-Chief or Strategist should decide whether it runs as long-form; if not, it becomes the 13:00 retatrutide lead Short. Two Shorts are possible from different angles: the efficacy result, and the side effects plus 'tirzepatide hasn't been tested against it yet' (TRIUMPH-5 is still pending). Second new opportunity: a Mayo retrospective cohort of 2,379 women aged 45+ (Menopause Society meeting; Healio Oct 23, MedPage Oct 27). Menopause hormone therapy was linked to more weight loss on semaglutide, but on tirzepatide the extra benefit was small and only lasted to 3 months. That makes an honest, calm question for women 45+, an audience we underserve. Fresh hooks for the Lane A queue: the 12-month real-world tirzepatide study (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 28) for the plateau video, and the Metabolites regain review for the stopping video. The tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder scoping review (Oct 23) suits the 08:00 body-worry Short. Upcoming: ObesityWeek (Washington DC, Nov 14–17). Novo has said it will present new CagriSema and Wegovy data there, so plan Lane C capacity. Thanksgiving content will peak around Nov 20–26. Rejected: compounded 'cheapest tirzepatide' listicles, 'retatrutide cost per milligram for research buyers', and microdosing (Yahoo, Oct 29). Lilly earnings, employer coverage and Medicare stories are banned lanes and are left out.

candidates.angle: Lane C candidate. Title idea (52 chars): 'Retatrutide vs Semaglutide: What the New Trial Found'. First sentence answers it: in adults with type 2 diabetes, retatrutide lowered A1C more and roughly doubled the weight loss of semaglutide 2 mg at 80 weeks. Then explain what it means. Make clear it is topline, not peer-reviewed and open-label. Weight results use the 'if everyone stayed on treatment' measure. The population is type 2 diabetes only. Give the side-effect trade-off: discontinuation 7.9% on 12 mg vs 2.7%; dysesthesia 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%. Close the loop with what still isn't known: no head-to-head against tirzepatide yet (TRIUMPH-5 pending), and it isn't approved. Carry the prescriber line and 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'. TIMING: the Oct 30 14:00 ET slot is about 55 h after first report, just past the 48 h rule, and there's no tirzepatide arm. EIC or Strategist decides. Otherwise it runs as the 13:00 retatrutide Short.

candidates.angle: 13:00 lead Short, honest uncertainty with a loop ending. 'More weight loss, but what did people feel?' Nausea was similar in both groups (about 21–24% vs 21%). Diarrhea was a bit higher on retatrutide (28–33% vs 26%). Skin-sensation reports (dysesthesia) and stopping were higher. End on the open question: has it been tested against tirzepatide? Not yet; TRIUMPH-5 is running. Tirzepatide-first phrasing isn't possible because tirzepatide wasn't in this trial, so lead with retatrutide. Say 'not yet peer-reviewed'.
